response.summary: The user learned how to downsample Lantern's 30-second readings without losing peaks and settled on 5-minute and 1-hour continuous aggregates that store mean, max and min.

facts.text: Lantern will keep 5-minute and 1-hour continuous aggregates storing mean, max and min per bucket.
Raw readings will be compressed after seven days.
Tariff changes will be marked on graphs as Grafana annotations.
Averaging 30-second readings into 5-minute buckets hides short spikes such as a kettle.
Keeping mean, max and min per bucket preserves peaks when graphing: draw the mean as a line and the max as a faint band.
LTTB (largest triangle three buckets) picks visually important points instead of averaging.
Continuous aggregates maintain bucketed statistics automatically as new readings arrive.
The Timescale toolkit extension ships an lttb() function.
Has a plugin for LTTB downsampling.
Annotations can mark events such as deploys or tariff changes on graphs.
Her law firm's IT team uses Grafana annotations to mark deploys.

decisions.question: How should Lantern downsample readings for graphs?
options: Mean, max and min per bucket in continuous aggregates
decisions.chosen: Mean, max and min per bucket in 5-minute and 1-hour continuous aggregates
decisions.reasoning: Peaks stay visible as a band above the mean and Timescale maintains the buckets automatically.
